Purpose: "Lynch at scale" means AI reads every filing and concall, tracks management promise-vs-delivery over years and spots changes early, while the human does real-world scuttlebutt. This note covers what data can actually be pulled from here (tested with curl from a cloud, non-Indian IP, on 2026-11-19), and which methods are backed by research.
Research, not SEBI-registered advice.

title: edge_methods_data_access › Edge methods and data access for Indian small caps (tested 2026-11-19)

body:
- **Calls read:** 10 concall transcripts, every quarter from Q1FY25 (30-Jul-2024) to Q2FY27 (30-Oct-2026). All came from NSE via `tools/nse_fetch.py transcripts SKIPPER --download` and were converted with `pdftotext`. Every call was read in full, not keyword-searched.
- **Promises extracted:** 68 forward-looking promises. For each one the ledger records the call date, speaker, exact quote, metric, target, deadline, specificity (precise / range / vague), materiality (1-3), and whether it was volunteered or prompted by an analyst.
- **Checking delivery:** each promise was checked against later calls (company-reported numbers) and screener.in consolidated data (P&L, quarterly results, balance sheet, ratios, and the "Other Assets" schedule for receivables), fetched 19-Nov-2026.
- **Speakers:** nearly every promise came from **Sharan Bansal** (Director/ED). The CFO (Shiv Shankar Gupta) gave one (the two-year >25% closing statement, Jul-24) and IR (Aditya Dujari) gave one (polymer INR 1,000 cr, Jul-24).

**Scoring rule.** These are the thresholds I used, stated up front:

| Status | Rule | Score |
|---|---|---|
| delivered | ≥ 95% of target (low end of a range), on time | +1 |
| partly | 80-95% of target, or at most 1 quarter late | +0.5 |
| missed | < 80% of target, or more than 1 quarter late | −1 |
| moved-goalpost | target or date changed at a later call without acknowledging the change | −1.5 |
| withdrawn | explicitly lowered, with an explanation | −0.5 |
| silently-dropped | not repeated for 4 or more calls | −1.5 |
| pending | deadline not yet reached | not scored |
| unverifiable | deadline passed, but no public number to check | not scored |

- **Weights** = specificity (precise 3 / range 2 / vague 1) × materiality (1-3) × recency decay (half-life 8 quarters).
- **Headline delivery ratio** = weighted share of credit, where delivered = 1, partly = 0.5 and everything else = 0.

body:
`insight:governance-surfacing-sequence` · confidence: verified

In the severe/poor cases reviewed, outside parties found the problem years before the regulator ruled on it, and the signals tended to arrive in this order. (1) Financing and structure: promoter pledges rising, ICDs or 'general purpose corporate loans' to opaque entities (RHFL to ADAG shells, SEBI 2024; DHFL's 'Bandra Book', SEBI 2025: ~Rs 14,040 cr; Fortis ICDs 2017-18), listed assets securing group debt (Zee, Jaypee), thin float after relisting (Ruchi/Patanjali 2020). (2) Credit market: rating downgrades, CP/NCD rollovers failing, lender 'fraud' tags (SBI on RCom 2025; PNB on Srei 2022), or forged no-default letters (Gensol, 2025). (3) Gatekeepers: auditor qualifications or resignations, delayed accounts (Byju's FY21 ~18 months late; Deloitte quit Jun-2023), independent directors leaving, a forensic auditor reporting non-cooperation (Rajesh Exports, per SEBI's 3-Jun-2026 interim order). (4) Bank regulator signals: RBI divergences and refusal of a CEO's term (Yes Bank 2016-18), RBI special audits (Srei), supersession. (5) Outsiders: whistleblowers (Videocon 2016), investigative media (Cobrapost on DHFL 2019), short sellers (Hindenburg on Adani 2023, Viceroy on Vedanta 2025). The short-seller claims were largely not upheld by SEBI in Adani's case, so on their own they are prompts for diligence, not verdicts. (6) Regulators and agencies act last: SEBI interim orders, then ED/CBI, often 2-7 years later. Counter-example: Infosys (2019 whistleblower allegations not substantiated after an independent probe; stock recovered). Process rule: any one of items 1-3 means a deeper check; two together means exit or don't enter.

Sources: <https://www.moneylife.in/article/dhfls-bandra-book-scam-sebi-slaps-rs120-crore-fine-bans-4-wadhawans-2-others-for-diverting-rs14000-crore-loan/77969.html> · <https://www.business-standard.com/companies/news/rhfl-fund-diversion-case-5-year-market-ban-for-anil-ambani-24-others-124082300983_1.html> · <https://www.businesstoday.in/markets/stocks/story/bt-explainer-what-sebis-interim-order-against-rajesh-exports-and-its-promoter-reveals-534811-2026-06-04> · <https://business-standard.com/markets/news/sebi-bars-gensol-engineering-promoters-for-alleged-fund-diversion-125041501266_1.html> · <https://www.business-standard.com/markets/news/sebi-clears-adani-group-dismisses-hindenburg-allegations-125091801259_1.html>

body:
- Coforge is the only explicit guider in the set: EBIT, EBITDA, FCF/PAT and ETR numbers, raised or restated almost every call, with a CEO script that cites its own past promises ('made sure they came true').
- Hard financial guidance was met or beaten: FY26 EBIT 14.4% vs 14%; Q4FY26 16.6% vs 15%; FCF/PAT 110% vs 70-80%; Encora closed inside the Mar-Apr 2026 window.
- The misses are softer statements: 'H2 should be robust' then a 2.0% CC Q4; a Q3 wage hit described as 'very, very limited' that cost 150 bp; the Cigniti merger ~2-3 months after 'December, January' (NCLT timetable, acknowledged); normalised ETR 23% vs 23.5-24%.
- FY27 is pending: EBITDA 20.5-21% (H1 20.5%), EBIT raised 15.5% -> 16% (H1 16.0%), FCF/PAT 100% (H1 92%), no EPS dilution from Encora. Reported growth is inflated by Encora from May-2026, so 'industry growth leader' needs an organic read.
title: COFORGE › 3. Reading

body: IT mid-cap managements almost always hit their **near-term margin guidance**: pooled delivery 98% (n=8). That covers EBIT/EBITDA bands, quarter-ahead margin walks and FY margin targets. These are levers management controls (utilisation, sub-contracting, ESOP cost, hedges). **Growth-shape, vertical and timing statements are much weaker:** 69% on revenue/growth (n=11, the same as auto components' 69%) and 82% on "other" (n=8). The other category covers DSO, tax rate, FCF, M&A dates and deal counts. The misses: Mphasis's Logistics recovery and DSO normalisation, Coforge's "robust H2" and Cigniti date, KPIT's "meaningful" Q4. **But the scores look better than the sector really is, because the big FY27 tests are all pending.** KPIT guided FY27 EBITDA at 20.5–21.2% in May-2026 and printed 17.2% and 17.8% in the next two quarters. Persistent re-cast "USD 2 bn revenue by FY27" as a Q4 exit run rate, and "+200–300 bp" as "16–17%", without saying either had changed. With 4–10 scored promises per company, the call rule shrinks everything hard. Only Mphasis gets a noticeable adjustment (−8 pts).

Anchored EV (gate) / size after gates. Fix (1) = proposed v1.6 EV convention (gate = mean of the outcome distribution).
Hurdle 1.762x India, 1.469x US.

| Card | Today (v1.5) | + fix 3 | + fix 1 | + fix 1 + fix 3 | info: fix 1 + 3 + 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AUTOAXLES | 1.40 / 0 | 1.66 / 0 | 1.49 / 0 | 1.75 / 0 | 2.04 / 4.0% |
| HARSHA | 1.58 / 0 | **1.87 / 4.0%** | 1.66 / 0 | **1.94 / 4.0%** | 2.12 / 4.0% |
| INDRAMEDCO | 1.39 / 0 | 1.58 / 0 | 1.45 / 0 | 1.64 / 0 | 1.83 / 0.8% (survival cap ≤1%) |
| SHK | 1.59 / 0 | 1.48 / 0 ¹ | 1.69 / 0 | 1.58 / 0 | 1.92 / 1.9% |
| SUNFLAG ² | 1.44 / 0 | 1.96 / 1.0% | 1.55 / 0 | 2.08 / 1.0% | 2.21 / 1.0% |
| — with india_nonfin class | 1.37 / 0 | 1.61 / 0 | 1.48 / 0 | 1.72 / 0 | 1.77 / 0.1% |
| UTKARSHBNK | 1.23 / 0 | 1.38 / 0 | 1.31 / 0 | 1.45 / 0 | 2.21 / 2.0% |
| UTTAMSUGAR | 0.89 / 0 | 1.30 / 0 | 0.95 / 0 | 1.36 / 0 | 1.37 / 0 |
| US-KEX ³ | 1.12 / 0 | 1.12 / 0 | 1.17 / 0 | 1.17 / 0 | 1.43 / 0 |

¹ SHK: the 5-point Gauss-Hermite grid puts 22.7% of mass at ≥3x vs the continuous model's 13.6%, so anchoring to 17.4%
*lowers* it — a quadrature artefact. A fix-3 patch should anchor on a finer grid (≥ 20 points) or the continuous tail.
² SUNFLAG names the deprecated survivor class (P(≥3x) 44% placeholder), which inflates two-sided anchoring; on the
correct class it stays 0. ³ US-KEX names a deprecated class with null tails → no anchoring at all (housekeeping fix 6).
- With only the fix that passed (3), **one live card would open: HARSHA at the 4% cap** (EV 1.87x; its gap was the smallest
  in the audit). With fix 1 too, still only HARSHA. The fix-4 column shows why σ matters more after fix 1: the mean of a
  lognormal is median·e^{σ²/2}, +6% at σ 0.35 but +26% at 0.68, so σ becomes an EV lever — another reason not to adopt it
  without a passed test.
- Under fix 1 alone, 7 of 8 live cards would get the new shape warning (all but HARSHA).
